title: Grammar Drills Now Follow What You Just Heard | vitalii.no
description:
Grammar breaks used to come from a fixed textbook order - now they're built from the exact sentences you just heard, with a real pause before the answer.

Grammar breaks used to follow a fixed textbook sequence, so the rule you heard might have nothing to do with the sentences you'd just spent 10 or 20 minutes listening to - it simply came from wherever the syllabus was. Worse, the drill spoke one explanation and moved straight into a fill-in exercise with no pause, so learners would catch themselves reading the answer instead of trying to recall it, and the typical mistake was never actually named out loud.

grammar_block() in runner.py now reads the last 48 sentences of the section just heard and passes them to Claude as context. A new grammar kind called "heard" lets the model build a drill from the grammar of those exact words when no fixed syllabus unit fits better, alongside existing chapters and six new B2/C1 nuance units. The explanation itself is now five spoken steps - why, the form, the typical mistake struck through as wrong, contrasts, and a summary - voiced by separate Ukrainian and Norwegian voices so no Norwegian word gets read in the wrong accent. Every drill item now waits 2.5 seconds plus 45 milliseconds per answer character before playing the answer.

The grammar break now audibly follows from the lesson instead of an arbitrary syllabus slot, names the actual mistake before contrasting it, and gives a real pause to answer instead of reading straight through - with B2/C1 learners getting nuance drills instead of the same beginner tables.
